correctness.rationale: Here V₂ is the ℓ² norm of first cyclic differences, not a second derivative. Replacing complex f by |f| only decreases the denominator and preserves the numerator; constant modulus gives zero numerator. For nonconstant modulus, subtracting its minimum within the nonnegative cone and rescaling are legitimate because all averages shift equally and the variation kills constants. At C₃ the maximal values at (u+v,v,0) reduce to the two cases in the proof; symbolic expansion verifies the energy identities, including equality for u≥v. At C₄ rotation and reflection place a maximum 1 at zero and a minimum 0 either adjacent or opposite, covering ties as well. An independent exact calculation generates averages from intervals in a doubled list, obtains the active cells by intersecting pairs of supporting lines and testing all constraints, and minimizes the quadratic deficit over vertices, all feasible vertex-to-vertex segments, and feasible positive-definite critical points. Only closures of full-dimensional cells are needed by continuity, since nonidentical affine ties lie on finitely many lines. An interior stationary point with an indefinite Hessian cannot be a minimum; if the Hessian is positive semidefinite but singular, a null line carries the same minimum value to the boundary. Linear or concave edge restrictions take a minimum at an endpoint. Thus the candidate list is exhaustive, not a grid scan. The replay gives six and seven cells with respective minima −1/12+5√13/156>0 and 0, and directly verifies the active witness averages and the squared ratio (7+√13)/36>1/4. Hence both constants are sharp in the stated domain.
residual_risks: Exact continuous optimization only for C₃ and C₄, with the prescribed operator and cyclic edge seminorm. No monotonicity at larger cycle sizes is inferred.

value.rationale: The sharp cyclic first-difference ratio is a natural stability quantity for uncentered maximal averaging. The first nontriangle cycle changes the arrangement of contiguity and creates a provable strict increase, with a non-indicator optimizer that improves on all indicators. The globally sharp algebraic constant and realizing pattern distinguish a genuine cyclic and amplitude effect from the previously studied centered, vertex-norm or indicator results. This is an independently useful exact small-cycle benchmark, not a claim about arbitrary cycle sizes.
residual_risks: The result does not characterize all four-cycle maximizers or the size dependence beyond four sites.
